statement.text:
An isometric action of a group G on a metric space S is called acylindrical if for
every ε > 0 there exist R, N > 0 such that for every two points x, y with d(x, y) ⩾ R,
there are at most N elements g ∈ G satisfying d(x, gx) ⩽ ε and d(y, gy) ⩽ ε. A
group is said to be acylindrically hyperbolic if it is not virtually cyclic and admits
an acylindrical action on a hyperbolic space with unbounded orbits. Is the automor-
phism group of a finitely generated acylindrically hyperbolic group also acylindrically
hyperbolic?                                                                 A. Genevois
